name: AI capex
cardDescription: The compute, memory, networking, power, and platform layer behind the AI buildout.
description: A research map of the public companies exposed to AI infrastructure spending, from accelerators and memory to power, cooling, and software monetization.
resilienceNote: NVIDIA, memory, and networking are tightly linked to AI spending. Power, electrical equipment, and reliable generation can benefit from broader infrastructure demand even if AI progress slows.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Direct accelerator and rack-scale-system exposure; benefits across GPUs, networking, and software.
candidates.failureCase: Custom ASICs, TPUs, cheaper inference, or a hyperscaler capex slowdown.

candidates.benefitMechanism: HBM and DRAM content rises with every high-end AI accelerator.
candidates.failureCase: HBM oversupply or memory prices collapsing after capacity expansion.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Manufactures advanced chips and packaging for NVIDIA, AMD, and hyperscaler ASICs.
candidates.failureCase: Taiwan risk, yield problems, customer insourcing, or AI demand weakness.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Custom AI ASICs, Ethernet switching, networking silicon, and optical connectivity.
candidates.failureCase: A major customer delays its ASIC program or cuts networking spending.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Power distribution, UPS, cooling, and thermal systems become more valuable as rack density rises.
candidates.failureCase: Data-center capex slows or customers shift to competing cooling architectures.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Etch and deposition equipment is needed for advanced logic, HBM, and 3D memory expansion.
candidates.failureCase: The memory capex cycle reverses and Samsung, SK Hynix, or Micron cut orders.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Ethernet switching for large AI clusters; benefits if open networking gains share.
candidates.failureCase: NVIDIA’s proprietary networking wins or hyperscaler capex slows.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Switchgear, breakers, busways, and power management for data centers and grid upgrades.
candidates.failureCase: Electrical-equipment orders normalize or projects face permitting delays.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Monetizes both Azure compute and enterprise AI/Copilot usage, with substantial funding capacity.
candidates.failureCase: Copilot adoption disappoints while AI capex damages margins and cash flow.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Google Cloud, Gemini, Search, and internally designed TPUs provide several ways to capture AI value.
candidates.failureCase: AI answers reduce profitable search activity faster than Cloud and Gemini grow.

watchlist.benefitMechanism: Data-center cooling exposure with a smaller scale than the major infrastructure names.
watchlist.failureCase: Execution risk, slower customer spending, or a weaker capex cycle.

watchlist.benefitMechanism: Optical transceivers and 1.6T connectivity offer high growth with meaningful execution risk.
watchlist.failureCase: Execution risk, slower customer spending, or a weaker capex cycle.

watchlist.benefitMechanism: Grid and transmission construction gives direct exposure to the power bottleneck.
watchlist.failureCase: Execution risk, slower customer spending, or a weaker capex cycle.

watchlist.benefitMechanism: Nuclear power and reliable generation can support AI campuses.
watchlist.failureCase: Execution risk, slower customer spending, or a weaker capex cycle.

watchlist.benefitMechanism: Data-center and interconnection rent capture, with rate sensitivity.
watchlist.failureCase: Execution risk, slower customer spending, or a weaker capex cycle.

watchlist.benefitMechanism: Data-center and interconnection rent capture, with rate sensitivity.
watchlist.failureCase: Execution risk, slower customer spending, or a weaker capex cycle.

name: Energy
cardDescription: Electricity demand, grid bottlenecks, nuclear reliability, natural gas, and infrastructure buildout.
description: The strongest energy angle is bigger than oil prices: power demand is colliding with a slow-moving grid, creating opportunities across generation, transmission, equipment, fuel, and gas infrastructure.
resilienceNote: CEG, PWR, ETN, and VST can benefit even if AI progress slows because grid reliability and electricity infrastructure have wider demand drivers. MOD, GEV, and other data-center-linked names are more exposed to an AI-capex digestion cycle.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Existing nuclear fleet can supply reliable power to AI data centers.
candidates.catalyst: Long-term power contracts and demand for firm generation.
candidates.failureCase: Contracts fail to produce attractive margins or nuclear outages increase.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Builds transmission, substations, and grid infrastructure required for new power demand.
candidates.catalyst: $44B backlog and roughly 70% of revenue from utility and power work.
candidates.failureCase: Permitting and interconnection delays slow backlog conversion.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Sells switchgear, breakers, busways, and power-management systems.
candidates.catalyst: Data-center and grid-upgrade orders compound over time.
candidates.failureCase: Data-center and electrical orders normalize after overbuilding.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Gas turbines, grid equipment, and electrification systems support rising power demand.
candidates.catalyst: Turbine, grid, and electrification backlog conversion.
candidates.failureCase: Turbine orders are delayed or renewable and storage economics improve faster.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Dispatchable generation and retail power exposure create leverage to scarcity pricing.
candidates.catalyst: Power scarcity and a recovery after a roughly 19% one-month drawdown.
candidates.failureCase: High leverage and falling power prices damage cash flow.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Uranium supply supports the expected expansion of nuclear power.
candidates.catalyst: Long-cycle nuclear demand and uranium contracting.
candidates.failureCase: Nuclear projects remain delayed or uranium prices fall.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Large renewable, storage, and utility-development platform.
candidates.catalyst: Renewable deployment, storage growth, and utility investment.
candidates.failureCase: Higher rates and project costs reduce renewable returns.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Natural-gas pipelines can supply gas-fired generation and industrial load.
candidates.catalyst: Growing gas demand from power generation and industrial projects.
candidates.failureCase: Gas demand disappoints or regulation limits new infrastructure.

candidates.benefitMechanism: LNG export capacity benefits from global gas demand and power scarcity.
candidates.catalyst: Export growth and global demand for flexible gas supply.
candidates.failureCase: LNG prices fall or export growth is restricted.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Thermal-management and cooling systems support high-density data centers.
candidates.catalyst: Data-center cooling demand and higher rack density.
candidates.failureCase: Customers adopt competing cooling designs or capex slows.

name: Healthcare
cardDescription: GLP-1s, diagnostics, life-sciences software, devices, and drug-development infrastructure.
description: Healthcare combines structural demand with very different risk profiles: recurring software and diagnostics, procedure growth, drug pipelines, and payer economics.
resilienceNote: The key failure modes are drug-price regulation, clinical failures, payer pressure, patent cliffs, and GLP-1 competition. DXCM, VEEV, and TMO offer a more balanced research starting point than the highest-multiple drug and robotics names.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Obesity and diabetes drugs, especially the GLP-1 franchise, expand into a huge metabolic-health market.
candidates.catalyst: Capacity expansion and new obesity indications.
candidates.failureCase: Pricing pressure, safety issues, or stronger competition.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Continuous glucose monitoring expands beyond insulin users and into metabolic health.
candidates.catalyst: New product launches and broader reimbursement.
candidates.failureCase: Insurance restrictions or cheaper competing sensors.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Life-sciences software benefits from digitized trials, compliance, and AI workflows.
candidates.catalyst: Vault expansion and AI-enabled workflows.
candidates.failureCase: Pharma customers reduce software spending or build internally.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Robotic surgery adoption increases procedure volume and recurring instrument revenue.
candidates.catalyst: More procedures, systems, and international adoption.
candidates.failureCase: Hospitals delay capital purchases or cheaper robots gain share.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Instruments, reagents, and services support drug development and biotech labs.
candidates.catalyst: Biotech funding and pharma R&D recovery.
candidates.failureCase: Weak biotech funding or lab-budget cuts.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Wegovy, Ozempic, and Rybelsus give Novo broad global obesity and diabetes exposure.
candidates.catalyst: Oral obesity drugs and manufacturing capacity.
candidates.failureCase: Lilly competition, pricing pressure, or disappointing trial data.

candidates.benefitMechanism: An aging population supports healthcare-services demand across insurance and care delivery.
candidates.catalyst: Medical-cost normalization and Optum growth.
candidates.failureCase: Medical-cost inflation, regulation, or reimbursement cuts.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Diagnostics, medical devices, diabetes monitoring, and nutrition diversify the growth engine.
candidates.catalyst: Device and glucose-monitoring growth.
candidates.failureCase: Product recalls or slower device growth.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Biologic medicines and an oncology and eye-care pipeline create multiple shots on goal.
candidates.catalyst: Pipeline approvals and label expansion.
candidates.failureCase: Clinical failures or biosimilar erosion.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Insurance, pharmacy, and healthcare delivery integration can compound when costs are controlled.
candidates.catalyst: Cost-control and insurance-margin recovery.
candidates.failureCase: Weak Medicare Advantage economics or debt pressure.

name: Defense
cardDescription: Missile replenishment, air defense, cyber, autonomy, space, and long-duration programs.
description: Defense spending is moving through missiles, air defense, naval programs, cyber, intelligence, autonomy, and space rather than a single equipment cycle.
resilienceNote: Political budget changes, fixed-price contract losses, procurement delays, labor shortages, and export restrictions remain the main risks. NOC, CACI, and GD offer a quality and value starting point; KTOS, AVAV, and PLTR carry more beta.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Missiles, air defense, avionics, and Pratt & Whitney engines cover several defense demand pools.
candidates.catalyst: Missile replenishment and defense-budget growth.
candidates.failureCase: Engine problems, delays, or cost overruns.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Strategic deterrence, space, missile defense, and autonomous systems provide long-duration program exposure.
candidates.catalyst: Long-duration U.S. defense programs.
candidates.failureCase: Program cancellations or execution problems.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Intelligence, cyber, electronic warfare, and mission software support modern defense operations.
candidates.catalyst: Government contract wins and acquisitions.
candidates.failureCase: Contract delays or budget cuts.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Submarines, armored vehicles, munitions, and IT services diversify defense exposure.
candidates.catalyst: Submarine and munitions demand.
candidates.failureCase: Shipbuilding delays and labor shortages.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Drones, hypersonics, missile systems, and autonomous platforms offer high-beta program exposure.
candidates.catalyst: Drone and hypersonic program awards.
candidates.failureCase: High valuation with weak profitability or program delays.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Missiles, air defense, F-35, space, and hypersonics anchor strategic programs.
candidates.catalyst: Missile replenishment and allied rearmament.
candidates.failureCase: Slow growth, fixed-price contracts, or budget pressure.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Small drones and loitering munitions connect battlefield lessons to procurement demand.
candidates.catalyst: Battlefield-proven drone demand.
candidates.failureCase: Competition, procurement delays, or weak margins.

candidates.benefitMechanism: AI-enabled defense and intelligence software can spread across U.S. and allied customers.
candidates.catalyst: U.S. government and allied adoption.
candidates.failureCase: Extreme valuation or customers choosing internal systems.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Nuclear submarines, carriers, and naval shipbuilding support fleet modernization.
candidates.catalyst: Submarine and fleet-modernization spending.
candidates.failureCase: Shipyard delays, labor shortages, or contract penalties.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Nuclear reactors, naval propulsion, and advanced nuclear components support strategic programs.
candidates.catalyst: Naval nuclear demand and microreactors.
candidates.failureCase: Program delays or cost overruns.

name: Financials
cardDescription: Exchanges, payments, asset managers, private credit, and diversified banking platforms.
description: Financial infrastructure earns from the flow of money: payments, trading, clearing, data, capital markets, asset gathering, and lending at scale.
resilienceNote: Credit losses, a yield-curve reversal, commercial-real-estate stress, regulation, and funding-market problems are the main cross-theme risks. V, MA, and ICE lead on quality; JPM, GS, and COF lead on valuation; BX and BLK connect to infrastructure financing.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Exchanges, data, clearing, and mortgage infrastructure monetize financial activity in several ways.
candidates.catalyst: Trading volumes, data growth, and mortgage recovery.
candidates.failureCase: Lower volatility or regulatory pressure.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Digital-payment volume grows with global consumption and the shift away from cash.
candidates.catalyst: Cross-border payments and cash-to-card conversion.
candidates.failureCase: Interchange regulation or new payment rails.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Commercial payments, cross-border spending, and network effects compound across the global economy.
candidates.catalyst: Commercial payments and international spending.
candidates.failureCase: Regulation or wallet and instant-payment competition.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Capital markets, trading, investment banking, and private credit benefit from deal activity.
candidates.catalyst: IPO and M&A recovery with higher trading activity.
candidates.failureCase: Credit losses or weak deal activity.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Scale banking, payments, cards, and investment banking create a broad earnings platform.
candidates.catalyst: Strong credit quality and capital-markets recovery.
candidates.failureCase: Recession, loan losses, or falling net-interest income.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Volatility and rate uncertainty increase futures, options, and clearing volumes.
candidates.catalyst: Higher trading volumes and new contracts.
candidates.failureCase: Calm markets or exchange-fee pressure.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Private credit and infrastructure financing capture growth in data centers and real assets.
candidates.catalyst: Fundraising and infrastructure AUM growth.
candidates.failureCase: Higher defaults, weak realizations, or fundraising slowdown.

candidates.benefitMechanism: ETF, index, private-market, and infrastructure assets scale on a global distribution platform.
candidates.catalyst: ETF and private-credit inflows.
candidates.failureCase: Fee compression or a broad market decline.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Consumer lending and the Discover integration create potential scale benefits.
candidates.catalyst: Integration synergies and credit normalization.
candidates.failureCase: Consumer defaults or integration problems.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Insurance float, cash, diversified operating businesses, and optionality create a durable financial base.
candidates.catalyst: Capital deployment after large cash accumulation.
candidates.failureCase: Poor succession execution or weak insurance results.

name: Cybersecurity
cardDescription: Identity, endpoint, network, cloud, data protection, and cyber recovery.
description: Security spending follows expanding attack surfaces, cloud adoption, regulation, and the rising cost of downtime across enterprises and governments.
resilienceNote: The theme has durable demand, but platform consolidation, breach-related reputational damage, and aggressive valuations can separate winners from the category.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Combines network, cloud, and security-operations products as enterprises consolidate vendors.
candidates.failureCase: Platform consolidation slows or large customers resist bundled pricing.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Cloud-native endpoint, identity, and threat-intelligence products benefit from recurring security workloads.
candidates.failureCase: Operational failures damage trust or Microsoft and other platforms take share.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Firewalls, secure networking, and security appliances protect distributed enterprise infrastructure.
candidates.failureCase: Appliance demand weakens or cloud-native rivals compress growth.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Cloud-delivered access controls replace legacy perimeter security for users, devices, and applications.
candidates.failureCase: Sales execution slips or customers delay large zero-trust projects.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Identity and access management sit at the control point for workforce and customer applications.
candidates.failureCase: Security incidents, pricing pressure, or Microsoft reduce new-logo growth.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Its global edge network bundles application security, developer services, and network performance.
candidates.failureCase: Edge services commoditize or infrastructure spending outruns monetization.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Subscription security, privacy, and identity products serve a large consumer installed base.
candidates.failureCase: Churn rises or free platform security reduces willingness to pay.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Automated endpoint detection and response can win customers seeking an independent security platform.
candidates.failureCase: Losses persist while larger competitors bundle comparable tools.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Data-security and recovery software benefits as ransomware makes resilient backups mission critical.
candidates.failureCase: Hyperscalers improve native recovery products or growth remains expensive.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Vulnerability, compliance, and asset-management tools help enterprises continuously measure cyber risk.
candidates.failureCase: Broader security platforms displace standalone vulnerability products.

name: Robotics & automation
cardDescription: Factory automation, machine vision, warehouses, surgical robots, and autonomy.
description: Labor scarcity, reshoring, quality control, and falling compute costs are pushing automation into factories, warehouses, hospitals, and farms.
resilienceNote: Automation can compound for years, while industrial cycles, customer concentration, and long payback periods make order timing uneven.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Semiconductor test systems and collaborative robots support more automated electronics production.
candidates.failureCase: Chip-test demand falls or collaborative robots fail to scale profitably.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Control systems, software, and services digitize factories and recurring industrial workflows.
candidates.failureCase: Industrial capex slows or customers delay large modernization projects.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Robotic-process automation software turns repetitive business workflows into programmable systems.
candidates.failureCase: AI-native tools displace legacy automation or enterprise expansion slows.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Vision systems let machines inspect, identify, and guide products at production speed.
candidates.failureCase: Consumer-electronics and logistics customers pause investment.

candidates.benefitMechanism: AI-driven storage and retrieval systems automate high-volume distribution centers.
candidates.failureCase: Customer concentration, deployment delays, or project economics disappoint.

candidates.benefitMechanism: A growing installed base drives recurring instruments and more robot-assisted procedures.
candidates.failureCase: Hospitals delay purchases or competing surgical systems gain adoption.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Process controls, warehouse systems, and aerospace automation span several mission-critical markets.
candidates.failureCase: Portfolio complexity and slow industrial orders limit growth.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Automation hardware and software improve uptime and efficiency in process industries.
candidates.failureCase: Energy and industrial customers defer projects or integration execution slips.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Scanning, tracking, and mobile-computing systems automate inventory and frontline workflows.
candidates.failureCase: Retail and logistics customers cut device-refresh budgets.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Precision agriculture and autonomous equipment raise farm productivity and software attachment.
candidates.failureCase: Farm income weakens or customers delay expensive equipment upgrades.

name: Water infrastructure
cardDescription: Pumps, treatment, smart metering, utilities, engineering, and drainage systems.
description: Aging networks, water scarcity, tighter quality standards, and climate adaptation require sustained investment across treatment, distribution, measurement, and reuse.
resilienceNote: Municipal and regulated spending can be durable, while project timing, public budgets, weather, and interest rates shape near-term returns.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Pumps, treatment, analytics, and smart-metering systems address the full water cycle.
candidates.failureCase: Municipal budgets tighten or integration and project execution disappoint.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Industrial water-treatment chemistry and services help customers reduce water and energy use.
candidates.failureCase: Industrial volumes soften or customers push back on pricing.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Pool, filtration, and flow-control products provide exposure to residential and commercial water systems.
candidates.failureCase: Housing and pool demand weaken or channel inventory rises.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Valves, controls, and treatment products improve safety and efficiency in buildings.
candidates.failureCase: Construction slows or input-cost pressure compresses margins.

candidates.benefitMechanism: The largest listed U.S. water utility can earn on long-lived network investment.
candidates.failureCase: Regulators limit allowed returns or financing costs remain elevated.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Water heaters and treatment products benefit from replacement demand and efficiency upgrades.
candidates.failureCase: China and North American housing demand weaken.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Hydrants, valves, and pipe products are essential to replacing aging municipal networks.
candidates.failureCase: Municipal projects slip or raw-material costs rise.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Connected meters and analytics help utilities find leaks, bill accurately, and manage scarce water.
candidates.failureCase: Utility adoption slows or premium valuation compresses.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Engineering and consulting services support treatment, remediation, and climate-resilience projects.
candidates.failureCase: Government awards slow or labor constraints pressure delivery.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Drainage pipe and water-management systems benefit from construction and resilience spending.
candidates.failureCase: Construction volumes fall or resin costs reduce margins.

name: Critical materials
cardDescription: Copper, rare earths, lithium, uranium, aluminum, and diversified mining.
description: Electrification, grid expansion, defense, batteries, and domestic supply policy are increasing the strategic value of materials with slow, concentrated supply chains.
resilienceNote: Scarcity can create pricing power, while commodity cycles, project delays, geopolitics, dilution, and cost inflation make the theme volatile.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Large copper assets provide direct exposure to grid, data-center, and electrification demand.
candidates.failureCase: Copper prices fall or major mine disruptions raise costs.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Long-life copper reserves can benefit from constrained supply and rising electrical demand.
candidates.failureCase: Political, permitting, or operating risk disrupts production.

candidates.benefitMechanism: U.S. rare-earth mining and magnet capacity support defense and supply-chain localization.
candidates.failureCase: Magnet ramp-up slips or Chinese pricing keeps margins weak.

candidates.benefitMechanism: A global lithium position benefits if battery demand absorbs current oversupply.
candidates.failureCase: Lithium prices remain depressed or expansion projects destroy returns.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Thacker Pass offers strategic domestic lithium exposure as production comes online.
candidates.failureCase: Construction, financing, permitting, or ramp-up setbacks dilute shareholders.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Uranium production and fuel services benefit from nuclear restarts and long-term contracting.
candidates.failureCase: Nuclear projects slip or uranium prices reverse.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Restartable U.S. uranium assets offer higher-beta exposure to domestic nuclear fuel demand.
candidates.failureCase: Production ramps slowly or equity dilution offsets commodity upside.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Domestic smelting capacity serves power, transport, and strategic manufacturing supply chains.
candidates.failureCase: Power costs rise or aluminum spreads compress.

candidates.benefitMechanism: A diversified base-metals portfolio benefits from electrification and constrained mine supply.
candidates.failureCase: Project execution slips or commodity prices weaken together.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Low-cost lithium and iodine assets provide scale across battery and industrial markets.
candidates.failureCase: Lithium oversupply, regulation, or contract changes reduce economics.

name: Space infrastructure
cardDescription: Launch, satellites, communications, earth observation, lunar systems, and payloads.
description: Cheaper launch and growing government demand are expanding the market for satellite networks, earth data, spacecraft components, and national-security space systems.
resilienceNote: Government contracts provide real demand, while launch failures, capital intensity, dilution, binary milestones, and unproven unit economics keep risk high.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Launch services, spacecraft, components, and government missions span more of the space stack.
candidates.failureCase: Launch setbacks, program delays, or valuation outrun execution.

candidates.benefitMechanism: A global low-earth-orbit network supports resilient voice, data, and government communications.
candidates.failureCase: Subscriber growth slows or replacement-satellite capex rises.

candidates.benefitMechanism: A satellite network aims to extend ordinary mobile coverage through carrier partnerships.
candidates.failureCase: Deployment, financing, spectrum, or technical milestones slip.

candidates.benefitMechanism: A large imaging constellation turns frequent earth data into subscriptions and analytics.
candidates.failureCase: Imagery commoditizes or commercial demand grows too slowly.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Power, structures, sensors, and in-space manufacturing serve civil and defense missions.
candidates.failureCase: Acquisitions, leverage, or program execution strain cash flow.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Lunar delivery, communications, and infrastructure contracts provide exposure to NASA's lunar buildout.
candidates.failureCase: Mission failures or contract timing create large revenue gaps.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Rapid satellite imagery and analytics support defense and intelligence customers.
candidates.failureCase: Constellation capex rises faster than contract wins.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Satellite capacity and secure communications serve aviation, government, and remote connectivity.
candidates.failureCase: Leverage, satellite failures, or low-earth-orbit competition erode returns.

candidates.benefitMechanism: A satellite constellation supplies weather, maritime, aviation, and tracking data through recurring services.
candidates.failureCase: Constellation costs rise faster than data-subscription growth.

candidates.benefitMechanism: Sensors, payloads, propulsion, and secure communications serve national-security space programs.
candidates.failureCase: Program delays, fixed-price costs, or defense priorities shift.
